prioritized_defects.description: The main flow skips the required mediator-to-local-PA handoff after choosing peers. R21 says the mediator instance passes the service requirements to the local PA to discover external resources from peers, but the diagram sends control from "Choose potential CDNs" directly to "Pass service requirements" and then to "Perform resource discovery" without an explicit local-PA handoff/action in the correct actor lane before the PA begins discovery.
prioritized_defects.evidence: R21 requires a mediator action that passes service requirements to the local PA to discover external resources. The diagram has N4 in lane "Mediator" labeled "Pass service requirements" and then immediately N5 in lane "Peering Agent" labeled "Perform resource discovery", but no explicit local-PA receive/pass step or equivalent handoff is shown, even though R116 indicates the PA receives service requirements from the mediator.
prioritized_defects.suggested_action: Insert or relabel an action that explicitly represents the mediator passing service requirements to the local PA, then start the PA discovery actions from that handoff.

prioritized_defects.description: The diagram uses an unsupported lane/actor for the policy branch: the decision and return action are placed in lane "Local PA", but the allowed swimlane names do not include Local PA. The requirements assign this behavior to the Local PA/PA, so the modeling should use one of the permitted lanes (typically "Peering Agent" or "Mediator" as appropriate) instead of an undeclared actor lane.
prioritized_defects.evidence: Requirements R25 and R128 state that the PA/local PA returns peering policies if they exist. The diagram models this branch in a lane named "Local PA", which is not one of the permitted swimlane names: Mediator, Peering Agent, Policy Agent, Service Registry, Policy Repository.
prioritized_defects.suggested_action: Move the decision and return action into a permitted lane that represents the PA, and keep the branch semantics unchanged.

prioritized_defects.description: The no-resources branch ends in a final node labeled "Renegotiation required", but the requirements say this branch should re-evaluate service requirements and send them back for re-negotiation, after which control continues to the earlier module rather than terminating the module with a special end state. This final node introduces an unsupported terminal outcome for a branch that is meant to loop back out of the module.
prioritized_defects.evidence: R133 says that if sufficient resources are not acquired, the mediator re-evaluates service requirements and sends them to the local PA to perform re-negotiation. The module instruction says only branches that stop or are rejected/cancelled/fail need their own final node; otherwise final nodes should pass control on. "Renegotiation required" is not a stated stop outcome here.
prioritized_defects.suggested_action: Replace the special final node with a control flow that exits this module to the re-negotiation entry path, or use the standard pass-on final if the module is meant to end here.

final_recommendation: Fix D2 first because it blocks the required handoff and workflow behavior, then D1 to correct the invalid actor/lane usage, and finally D3 to resolve the unsupported terminal outcome on the renegotiation branch.
